scope: Static analysis of publicly deployed application JavaScript only. No private data accessed and application code not executed.

status_labels.confirmed: Literal or AST structure present in public bundle; backend behavior is not validated.
status_labels.inferred: Frontend intent suggests this behavior; backend implementation not recovered.
status_labels.unknown: Not determinable from available public bundle.

notes: All endpoints are evidence of frontend intent/call sites, not confirmation of backend existence.
No application module was executed; source was parsed/formatted only. No private data was read and no authenticated API was invoked.

Vendor-named bundles, html2canvas, purify and index.es dependency chunks were excluded from contract discovery. Some application chunks embed SDK/dependency code; only application call sites were used.
Query cache-busters may be dynamic expressions. Payload types marked dynamic cannot be inferred safely from a minified variable alone.
Readable copies preserve the public Firebase client configuration present in the original artifact; reports intentionally omit client configuration values.

bffFetch.authorization: No Authorization header added by this wrapper. Cookie session transport is configured with credentials:include. Backend validation is unknown.

readability.method: prettier@3.8.0 babel parser, one output file per original application chunk, exact same filenames/imports/exports
readability.typescript_recovery: Original TS/TSX, symbol names, comments, dependency pins and original module boundaries are not recoverable exactly from these compiled chunks. Do not label formatted JS as original source.
readability.esbuild_alternative: Transform each chunk as ESM with minify:false, bundle:false, target:esnext, legalComments:preserve. Do not rename hashed import targets or re-bundle vendor chunks. Formatting with prettier is the lower-change choice.

unknowns: Original server/API implementation, complete deployed Functions inventory, runtime generation and service-account permissions.
Firestore/Storage security rules, deployed indexes and bucket IAM.
Actual data contents, installed production roles/users, configured Auth providers and authorized domains.
Original source tree, TypeScript types, original package manifest and exact dependency versions.
Which hosting rewrites route /api/* and /comments/react; frontend links imply these rewrites but do not reveal their deployed definitions.
Whether every API endpoint currently exists or returns the shapes the client expects.
No execution/authenticated validation of protected routes was performed by this analysis.
